The first published release since 4.3.1 in August. Everything from 4.4.0 to
4.15.3 was merged and never published, so if you're on 4.3.1 you get all of
it at once, under a new name, a new image, a new chart and a new license.
**Coming from 4.3.1, it is not a plain `helm upgrade`.** Read "Upgrading from
4.3.1" below before you touch a running plant.

The full notes are in the README:
What changed in 4.16.0,
and below it every version back to 4.4.0.

## In short

- **HotLoop Core: entities.** Every tag is an entity with a stable id, placed
  on an ISA-95 equipment tree. Motors, valves, PID loops and the rest are
  composites built from their tags, every alarm is an entity, and every entity
  command goes through the same write gate as a tag write. Agents (MCP),
  automations and the new Entities and Plant screens all use them. A service
  call can be asked first with `?dry_run=true`, and the command prompt tells
  you "Would be refused: ..." before you confirm.
- **Notifications that reach a phone:** ntfy and the Discord bot with an
  Acknowledge button, Gotify, and a Discord webhook, on rate limits that fold a
  flood into one summary.
- **Fixes that matter on a running plant:** unshelve could wipe an
  unacknowledged alarm; an OPC UA subscription could go silent forever while
  the session said connected; a silent Modbus device took up to 15 minutes to
  go down; a failed webhook logged its URL, which for Discord and ntfy is the
  password; restore loaded columns by position; every redeploy replaced the
  OPC UA server's certificate, so Ignition stopped trusting it; Discover tags
  imported every OPC UA node as a float; the Settings screen named poll
  variables that nothing reads.
- **Ignition 8.3.9 reads our OPC UA server**, verified end to end, and the
  server reports `HotLoop` as its manufacturer now.
- **The Edge Relay ships** as its own image and chart, in lockstep with the
  Gateway. TimescaleDB 2.30.1, and the extension updates itself now.

### API changes

- Empty lists are `[]`, never `null`, everywhere, streams included.
- `/api/history` buckets with no good reading are `null` (a gap), and bad
  readings stay out of averages.
- An error the API can't place is a 500 with a log ref, not a 400. A device
  that errors on a write or a browse is a 502.
- A service an alarm entity doesn't take (`alarm.turn_on`) is a 400. It used
  to answer success and do nothing.
- Unshelving an alarm that isn't shelved is a 409.
- Tag JSON always carries `minValue`, `maxValue` and `hasRange`.
- New: `?dry_run=true` on `POST /api/services/{domain}/{service}`. Only `true`
  or `false`; anything else is a 400.

### Upgrading from 4.3.1

- Image `ghcr.io/hotloop-io/hotloop` (was `ghcr.io/embernet-ai/industrial-iot`),
  chart repository `https://hotloop.io/hotloop`, chart `hotloop` (was
  `industrial-iot`), every `IIOT_` variable is `HOTLOOP_`.
- The chart name is in the workload selectors, which Kubernetes won't change
  in place. Keep the release name and namespace, then: `pg_dump` the
  database; delete the old Deployment (`<release>`) and StatefulSet
  (`<release>-postgresql`), which leaves the database volume where it is;
  `helm upgrade <release> hotloop/hotloop -f your-4.3.1-values.yaml`. Not
  `--reuse-values`. Rename any `IIOT_` in `extraEnv` and drop an
  `image.repository` override. The new database pod mounts the old volume
  and the Gateway migrates it forward on start.
- License: HotLoop's own license terms, not the ones 4.3.1 shipped with. Free
  for home and lab use; businesses sign up free through EmberNET. The current
  terms are in LICENSE.
- There is a login, writes default to off, and a timezone that won't load
  stops startup instead of running on UTC.
